sentences.text: Shri Arvind Singh - Government Advocate for the respond Heard on I.A. No.11566/2025 , second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.

His previous application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.04.2024.
2.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 24.11.2022 passed by Second Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO Act, Itarsi, District Narmadpuram (M.P.) in S.C.
No.10/2018, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
 Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine In lie  376(1) of IPC R.I. for 10 years Rs.500/- Additi  3/4 of POCSO Act R.I. for 10 years Rs.500/- Additi 5(j)(ii)/6 of POCSO Act R.I. for 20 years Rs.500/- Additional R.I. for two months 3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
As per prosecution case, the allegation against the appellant is that he committed sexual intercourse with the minor prosecutrix aged about 17 years.
Learned counsel submits that the trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly.

There was a love affair between the prosecutrix and the appellant and when it came to the knowledge of the parents of prosecutrix that she is pregnant, a false case has been 2 CRA-12371-2022 registered against the appellant.
Learned counsel further submits that Dr. Kelu Girwale (P.W.7) in her cross-examination has deposed that the prosecutrix has died due to excessive bleeding and blood clots during abortion.
Learned counsel further submits that the age of the prosecutrix i.e. 17 years at the time of the incident, is doubtful as the same has not been proved by the prosecution.
The prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses.
The appellant was on bail during trial and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.

He has already undergone almost three years of incarceration,
therefore, the application may be considered on the ground of period of incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6 . Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the overall facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.

7. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, 3 CRA-12371-2022 I.A.
No.11566/2025 is allowed.

8 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
9. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMAR   JUDGE JUDG  Shanu Brajesh Bamne vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157220048/
